title: Purify one sense
line: Seven days choosing what one sense lets in.
intro: For Athena, the philosopher purifies the senses rather than renouncing them: purifying means choosing what you let in, moving towards what benefits (ὠφέλιμον) and away from what harms (βλαβερόν). Athena’s test for each contact is three questions: what am I receiving, what satisfies me, what do I lose? For seven days you work with one sense, swapping one input that drags you down for one that lifts you.
does: For seven days, swap one input that drags you down for one that lifts you, through one sense.
trains: Choosing what reaches the soul, instead of taking whatever comes.
each: Keep to the sense you chose on day one. Swap one input that drags you down for one that lifts you: for hearing, no background news or television, and one harmonious piece listened to on purpose; for smell, no synthetic perfume or air freshener, and flowers, herbs or incense instead; for sight, no screen in bed, and ten minutes looking at a tree or the sky. With each contact, ask: what am I receiving, what satisfies me, what do I lose? In the evening, note what you took in.
note: What did you let in through this sense today, and what did it feed: did it lift you or drag you down?
end: After seven days, what has changed in what you reach for, and which swap will you keep?
